page.name: Receipt webhooks
page.h1: Push receipts to your own endpoint
page.metaTitle: Receipt webhooks to your own endpoint
page.metaDescription: Configure an endpoint per tenant and let the platform push delivery receipt events to it, instead of polling for status.
page.lede: Polling for status works until the volume makes it wasteful. A callback lets the system that cares about an event be told about it, which also means the record lands in your own database at the same time.

p: A callback endpoint is set per tenant, and the platform pushes receipt events to it as they are normalized. The destination is yours, so the event can be recorded, acted on, or fanned out internally without asking the platform again.
bullets: Receipt events pushed rather than polled
The event record also lives in your own system

p: A webhook is not a database write. Endpoints go down, deployments return errors, and a push can be lost — so design the handler to be idempotent and reconcile against the message log, which is the authoritative record.
bullets: Make the handler idempotent — the same event may arrive more than once
Reconcile against the logs rather than assuming every push arrived
Treat the callback as a fast path, not as your system of record

p: The events pushed are the ones the platform produces — delivery receipts that have been normalized into one status vocabulary, so your endpoint receives a stable value rather than a provider-specific word it has to interpret.

faq.q: How many times will a callback be retried?
faq.a: Treat the callback as best-effort: make the handler idempotent and reconcile against the message log, which is your record of truth. The callback guide sets out the model.

faq.q: Can I have more than one endpoint?
faq.a: The callback destination is configured per tenant. Fan-out to several internal consumers is something your own endpoint can do once it receives the event.

faq.q: Do webhooks cover email and WhatsApp?
faq.a: Where the provider reports delivery back, yes — every SMS provider we connect, Resend on email and Meta on WhatsApp. Those events are normalized into the same statuses and pushed to the same endpoint, so one handler covers them. Providers whose delivery events are not wired back yet are named on their /integrations/ pages.
